content.text:
## Ce que j'ai trouvé

**15 instances de `table.Model` réparties dans 8 packages**, toutes construites à la main :

| Package | Tables |
|---|---|
| `oci_resources` | `imageTable`, `networkTable`, `volumeTable`, `registryTable`, `tagTable` (browser), `table` (network inspect) |
| `status` | `monitorTable`, `sslTable` |
| `netdiag` | `resultsTable`, ports `table` |
| `containers`, `explorer`, `security`, `workspaces` | 1 chacune |

Ce qui est **déjà factorisé** : `theme.DefaultTableStyles()` / `TableStylesForState()` / `TableStylesForSeverity()`, `components.FilterBar`, `theme.TimeAgo`. Donc le style et le *widget* de filtre sont partagés — mais rien de la mécanique.

## Les 6 axes de duplication

**1. Arithmétique de largeur (Rule 116) — ~290 lignes, 12 copies**

`internal/ui/oci_resources/layout.go:51-131` (×4), `status/update.go:186-217` (×2), `containers/update.go:872-886`, `workspaces/view.go:54-96`, `security/findings.go:128-140`, `netdiag/ports_model.go:314-330`, `explorer/model.go:180-205`, `registry_browser.go:229-260`, `network_inspect_form.go:93-112`.

Toutes recalculent `available := width - 2 - numCols*2` puis répartissent. Et elles ne le font **pas de la même façon** : `status` et `containers` utilisent des pourcentages, `oci_resources` et `workspaces` du fixe+flex, `security` du fixe avec une seule colonne élastique. Le commentaire « la dernière colonne absorbe l'arrondi » est copié-collé 6 fois.

Pire, l'invariant `sum(widths) == available` est cassé silencieusement à `workspaces/view.go:83-85` : le clamp `if cols[10].Width < colModFixed` ajoute de la largeur après coup, donc sur terminal étroit la ligne sélectionnée dépasse la bordure.

**2. Tri — 3 implémentations quasi identiques**

`explorer/table.go:81-113`, `containers/update.go:631-667`, `oci_resources/table.go:33-67`. Même squelette exact :

```go
sorted := make([]T, len(items)); copy(sorted, items)
sort.Slice(sorted, func(i, j int) bool {
    var less bool
    switch m.sortColumn { /* ... */ }
    if m.sortAsc { return less }
    return !less
})
```

Seul le `switch` diffère. `cycleSort()` est dupliqué 3 fois à l'identique.

**3. Flèches de tri dans les headers — 3 copies verbatim**

`explorer/table.go:130-166`, `containers/update.go:800-832`, `oci_resources/table.go:130-148`. Y compris les deux maps `sortColIndex` / `baseTitles` et le bloc `arrow := " ▲"`.

**4. Application du filtre texte — 5 copies**

`workspaces/table.go:31-42`, `explorer/table.go:15-31`, `oci_resources/table.go:17-30`, `netdiag/ports_model.go:274-302`, `containers` (filteredContainers). Toutes font « lowercase la query, `strings.Contains` sur N champs ». Le `FilterBar` fournit la query, mais chaque vue réécrit le matching.

**5. Clamp du curseur — implémenté dans 2 vues sur 8**

`workspaces/table.go:69` et `explorer/table.go:54` ont le fix (avec le même commentaire explicatif copié). Les autres ne l'ont pas : `oci_resources` compense en appelant `GotoTop()` sur chaque toggle de filtre (`keys.go:56,127,158,192,224` — 5 sites), ce qui perd la position de scroll. `containers` et `status` ne font ni l'un ni l'autre.

**6. Résolution `curseur → objet métier` — 9 helpers `getSelectedX()`**

`containers/update.go:236`, `oci_resources/images.go:33`, `registries.go:14`, `resources.go:47,56`, `browser_state.go:97,106`, `status/update.go:230`. Chacun **rejoue le pipeline filtre+tri** pour retrouver l'élément :

```go
sorted := m.sortedImages(m.filteredImages())
return &sorted[m.imageTable.Cursor()]
```

C'est la duplication la plus dangereuse : si l'ordre de construction des lignes et celui de `getSelected` divergent, on agit sur le mauvais objet, sans erreur.

## Sur ton idée

Elle est juste, et l'argument le plus fort n'est pas le volume de code — c'est que **Rules 116 et 122 sont aujourd'hui des conventions vérifiées en revue, alors qu'un composant générique les rend structurellement invérifiables autrement**. Aujourd'hui rien n'empêche d'écrire `style.Render(...)` dans un `table.Row{}` ; avec un `Cell func(T) string` documenté comme « texte brut », le styling passe forcément par le chemin `SetStyles`.

Une nuance importante : `bubbles/table` prend des `[]table.Row` (des `[]string`). Une config purement déclarative (« nom, triable, largeur_min ») ne suffit pas — il faut que la colonne sache **extraire** sa valeur depuis le type métier. D'où des génériques, sinon on retombe sur `[]string` et les 9 `getSelectedX()` restent.

## Design proposé — `internal/ui/datatable`

```go
type Column[T any] struct {
    Title    string
    MinWidth int                      // largeur plancher
    Flex     int                      // 0 = fixe à MinWidth ; >0 = part du reliquat
    Cell     func(T) string           // texte brut — Rule 122 par construction
    Less     func(a, b T) bool        // nil = colonne non triable
    Search   func(T) string           // nil = colonne non cherchable
}

type Config[T any] struct {
    Columns     []Column[T]
    Tokens      []components.FilterToken
    TokenMatch  func(item T, active map[string]bool) bool
    DefaultSort int
    RowState    func(T) string        // -> theme.TableStylesForState/Severity
}

type Model[T any] struct { /* table.Model + FilterBar + items/filtered/sorted */ }

func New[T any](cfg Config[T]) Model[T]

func (m *Model[T]) SetItems(items []T)          // filtre + trie + rows + clamp curseur, en un point
func (m *Model[T]) Selected() (T, bool)         // remplace les 9 getSelectedX
func (m *Model[T]) SelectedIndex() int          // index dans les items d'origine
func (m *Model[T]) Resize(width, height int)    // Rule 116, une seule fois
func (m *Model[T]) Update(tea.Msg) (Model[T], tea.Cmd)  // ↑↓/jk, pgup/pgdn, g/G, `.`, `/`
func (m *Model[T]) View() string
func (m *Model[T]) FilterBar() *components.FilterBar     // pour RenderFooter / GetFooterHeight
func (m *Model[T]) InEditMode() bool
```

Le calcul de largeur devient un seul algorithme : `available = width - 2 - len(cols)*2`, on sert les `MinWidth`, on répartit le reliquat au prorata des `Flex`, la dernière colonne flexible absorbe l'arrondi — et l'invariant `sum == available` est testable une fois pour toutes.

Ce qui **reste dans les vues** : les colonnes et leurs extracteurs, les actions métier (`ctrl+d`, `ctrl+s`, `enter`), les tabs, les formulaires, le drill-down de l'explorer (le tri/filtre s'applique au niveau courant, ce qui marche déjà comme ça).

## Ce qui ne rentrera pas proprement

Trois cas à traiter à part plutôt que de tordre la config :

- **`status`** : deux tables qui partagent un viewport avec focus alterné (`DefaultTableStyles` / `BlurredTableStyles` selon l'onglet). Deux `datatable.Model` + un helper de focus, pas une abstraction « multi-table ».
- **`security/findings`** : filtrage par onglet *et* par sévérité, avant le filtre texte. Se modélise avec `TokenMatch`, mais le curseur doit repartir en haut au changement d'onglet — comportement différent de `SetItems` (qui préserve la position).
- **`netdiag` ports** : la reconstruction paresseuse (`tableReady` / `lastTableWidth`, `ports_model.go:346-378`) existe pour préserver le scroll sur un tick de 2s. C'est exactement ce que `SetItems` doit garantir par défaut — donc ce code disparaît, mais il faut le tester explicitement.

## Migration suggérée

Par ordre de risque croissant, une vue par PR :

1. `datatable` + tests (largeurs, clamp curseur, tri, filtre) — sans migrer personne
2. `oci_resources` réseaux + volumes (tables les plus simples, pas de tri)

5. `workspaces`, `explorer` (valident le clamp et le drill-down)
6. `security`, `status` (les deux cas particuliers)

Estimation : ~500 lignes supprimées des vues contre ~280 dans le composant, plus les tests. 1291	### 3.8 Docker registry groups
1292	
1293	Two shapes have to be supported: a remote registry with or without
1294	authentication, and a **group** fronting several remote registries, itself
1295	reachable anonymously or not. The second is the one the current model cannot
1296	express.
1297	
1298	Not started. The decisions below are settled; one is not, and is marked as such.
1299	
1300	#### What the current code does
1301	
1302	| Concern | Today | Where |
1303	|---|---|---|
1304	| Parent/child relation | in memory only, for the lifetime of one browser session | `registry_browser.go:26` (`browserRegistryEntry`) |
1305	| Group discovery | Nexus REST, re-run on **every** browser open, 8 s timeout each, behind a blocking spinner | `registry_browser.go:153`, `registrymgr/nexus.go` |
1306	| Member URLs | synthesised as `host + /repository/<memberName>`, alias stripped of `-proxy`/`-hosted`/`-local` | `nexus.go:111`, `nexus.go:200` |
1307	| Credential inheritance | member searches use the **parent's** URL as the `~/.docker/config.json` lookup key | `browser_keys.go:130` |
1308	| Registries tab | flat table, no indication a group was ever found | `table.go:182` |
1309	| Result filter (`r`) | cycles member URLs; no group level | `browser_tags.go:25` |
1310	
1311	`RegistryConfig.Registries` is a flat `[]RegistryItem` and carries no parent
1312	field. Nothing about a group survives closing the browser: it is rediscovered,
1313	over the network, next time.
1314	
1315	The credential inheritance is the one piece that already behaves correctly, and
1316	the reason it does is the same reason the open decision below is hard.
1317	
1318	#### Settled
1319	
1320	| Ref | Decision |
1321	|---|---|
1322	| A | **One list, one discriminator, one parent pointer** — `kind: registry \| group` plus `parent` on `RegistryItem`. Two parallel lists and a recursive `Children` tree were both rejected. |
1323	| 1 | The parent is referenced by **slug**, not by URL. |
1324	| 3 | Discovered members live in a **disk cache**, not in `config.yaml`. |
1325	| 4 | The Registries tab gets **drill-down** navigation (`←` / `→`), not an indented tree and not a `Group` column. |
1326	| 5 | **No purely logical groups.** A group always corresponds to a real repository-manager group. |
1327	| F | `provider` is a **declared field**, not sniffed from the URL. |
1328	
1329	**A — one list.** A Nexus group *is* a pullable registry as well as a container,
1330	so splitting `registries` and `registry_groups` would have duplicated the form,
1331	the table and the credential handling to model a distinction the server does not
1332	make. A single list with a discriminator keeps one table, one form (fields shown
1333	per `kind`), and leaves sorting and filtering intact.
1334	
1335	**1 — slug over URL.** The URL is today's de facto identifier and is threaded
1336	through `registryLoginStatus`, the scan cache keys and the message types, which
1337	is exactly why it is the wrong thing to hang a parent link on: editing a group's
1338	URL would silently orphan its members. The slug replaces the URL **only as the
1339	parent link and the cache key** — everything Docker-facing stays keyed on the
1340	URL, because that is what Docker itself is keyed on. Existing configs migrate by
1341	deriving a slug from the alias, falling back to the URL host; uniqueness has to
1342	be enforced at load, and the form needs to reject a collision rather than accept
1343	a config that will not round-trip.
1344	
1345	**3 — cache, not config.** Discovered members are derived data with a server as
1346	their source of truth, and `config.yaml` is what the user declares. Putting them
1347	in the cache mirrors `ImageScanCache` and `WorkspaceScanCache` (Rule 126) rather
1348	than inventing a fourth persistence shape:
1349	`~/.devdesk/cache/registry-groups.json`, keyed by group slug, refreshed
1350	explicitly with `ctrl+r` on a group row. The browser then reads config plus
1351	cache and opens instantly and offline, which is what removes D13's blocking
1352	state rather than papering over it. A `Members` column showing the count and
1353	`theme.TimeAgo(discovered_at)` (Rule 127) is what keeps staleness visible —
1354	without it, a silently stale cache is worse than the current re-detection.
1355	
1356	**4 — drill-down.** Level 1 lists groups and standalone registries; `→` enters a
1357	group and lists its members; `←` goes back, with a breadcrumb below the table
1358	(Rules 111, 123). The indented-tree alternative reads faster at five registries
1359	but breaks the moment the table is sorted or the FilterBar (Rule 136) narrows
1360	it, and drill-down is already the pattern `gitlab-explorer` uses. Proposed
1361	columns: `Alias | URL | Kind | Auth | Login | Members`.
1362	
1363	**5 — no logical groups.** Grouping unrelated registries under a user-invented
1364	name was considered and dropped: it has no server to discover from, no shared
1365	credential to inherit, and no group URL to pull through, so it would be a
1366	display-only concept carrying the weight of a real one. If the need for
1367	arbitrary grouping appears later it is a saved-selection feature in the browser,
1368	not a change to the registry model.
1369	
1370	**F — declared provider.** `NexusDetector.CanHandle` currently returns true
1371	whenever `ManagementURL` is non-empty (`nexus.go:31`), which makes that field do
1372	double duty as an implicit "this is Nexus" flag and makes the detector list
1373	effectively single-vendor. A `provider` field on the group — `nexus`, `harbor`,
1374	`artifactory`, `gitlab`, `generic` — turns `CanHandle` into a match on a
1375	declared value, with the generic detector last. It is a cycle field in the form
1376	(Rule 132) and it is what makes a second implementation possible without

### Table plumbing is written out again in every view

**15 `table.Model` instances across 8 packages, each wired by hand.** What is
shared today is the *look* — `theme.DefaultTableStyles()`,
`TableStylesForState/Severity()`, `components.FilterBar`, `theme.TimeAgo` — and
none of the mechanism. Column widths, sorting, sort arrows, filter matching,
cursor clamping and cursor-to-object resolution are re-implemented per view.

| Package | Tables |
|---|---|
| `oci_resources` | `imageTable`, `networkTable`, `volumeTable`, `registryTable`, `tagTable` (browser), `table` (network inspect) |
| `status` | `monitorTable`, `sslTable` |
| `netdiag` | `resultsTable`, ports `table` |
| `containers`, `explorer`, `security`, `workspaces` | one each |

#### What is duplicated

| Concern | Copies | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Column-width arithmetic (Rule 116) | 12, ~290 lines | `oci_resources/layout.go:51-131` (×4), `status/update.go:186-217` (×2), `containers/update.go:872-886`, `workspaces/view.go:54-96`, `security/findings.go:128-144`, `netdiag/ports_model.go:314-330`, `explorer/model.go:180-205`, `registry_browser.go:229-260`, `network_inspect_form.go:93-112` |
| Sort comparator scaffold | 3 | `explorer/table.go:81-113`, `containers/update.go:631-667`, `oci_resources/table.go:33-67` |
| Sort arrows in headers | 3, verbatim | `explorer/table.go:130-166`, `containers/update.go:800-832`, `oci_resources/table.go:130-148` |
| Text-filter matching | 5 | `workspaces/table.go:31-42`, `explorer/table.go:15-31`, `oci_resources/table.go:17-30`, `netdiag/ports_model.go:274-302`, `containers` `filteredContainers` |
| Cursor clamp on row shrink | 2 of 8 | present: `workspaces/table.go:69`, `explorer/table.go:54` — absent elsewhere |
| `getSelectedX()` | 9 | `containers/update.go:236`, `oci_resources/images.go:33`, `registries.go:14`, `resources.go:47,56`, `browser_state.go:97,106`, `status/update.go:230` |

The three sort comparators are the same eight lines around a different `switch`;
so are the three arrow blocks, down to the `sortColIndex` / `baseTitles` maps and
`arrow := " ▲"`. The five filter loops all lowercase the query and run
`strings.Contains` over N fields.

#### The width clamps break the invariant they exist to protect

Rule 116 requires `sum(col_widths) == available` so the selected row reaches the
right viewport border. Every site enforces it the same way — last column absorbs
the remainder — and then several add a per-column `max(…, floor)` *after* the
remainder is computed, which silently pushes the sum over `available`.

`workspaces/view.go` is the clearest case. With `numColumns = 11`,
`available = width - 24`, and 105 columns of fixed width, `Remote` clamps at 10
and `Modified` clamps at 15 (`view.go:64,83-85`). **Below a 154-column terminal
the widths sum to 130 against an `available` that is smaller** — 96 at width 120,
an overflow of 34. Same class at `security/findings.go:143` (below 72 columns),
`registry_browser.go:240` (`flexTag` floors at 8, so the last column can go
negative), `oci_resources/layout.go:66,89,108,123` and
`netdiag/ports_model.go:325`.

One solver that distributes the *shortfall* across flexible columns instead of
clamping each one independently removes the whole class. It is also the only way
to test the invariant once rather than eleven times.

#### The cursor is coupled to the pipeline by hand

Each `getSelectedX()` replays filter-then-sort to map a cursor back to a domain
object:

```go
sorted := m.sortedImages(m.filteredImages())
return &sorted[m.imageTable.Cursor()]
```

Nothing ties that ordering to the one `updateImageTable` used to build the rows.
If they drift, the action lands on the wrong object with no error. This is the
duplication worth removing on correctness grounds rather than volume.

The missing clamp is the same coupling seen from the other side: `oci_resources`
compensates with `GotoTop()` on every filter toggle
(`keys.go:56,127,158,192,224`), which throws away the scroll position;
`containers` and `status` do neither.

#### Proposed shape — `internal/ui/datatable`

`bubbles/table` takes `[]table.Row` (plain `[]string`), so a purely declarative
config cannot resolve a cursor back to a domain object — the column has to know
how to extract from `T`. Go 1.25, so generics are available:

```go
type Column[T any] struct {
    Title    string
    MinWidth int                 // floor
    Flex     int                 // 0 = fixed at MinWidth; >0 = share of the leftover
    Cell     func(T) string      // plain text — Rule 122 by construction
    Less     func(a, b T) bool   // nil = not sortable
    Search   func(T) string      // nil = not searchable
}

type Config[T any] struct {
    Columns     []Column[T]
    Tokens      []components.FilterToken
    TokenMatch  func(item T, active map[string]bool) bool
    DefaultSort int
    RowState    func(T) string   // -> theme.TableStylesForState / ForSeverity
}

func New[T any](cfg Config[T]) Model[T]

func (m *Model[T]) SetItems(items []T)         // filter + sort + rows + clamp, one path
func (m *Model[T]) Selected() (T, bool)        // replaces the nine getSelectedX
func (m *Model[T]) Resize(width, height int)   // Rule 116, once
func (m *Model[T]) Update(tea.Msg) (Model[T], tea.Cmd) // ↑↓/jk, pgup/pgdn, g/G, `.`, `/`
func (m *Model[T]) FilterBar() *components.FilterBar   // for RenderFooter / GetFooterHeight
func (m *Model[T]) InEditMode() bool
```

The point is not the line count — roughly 500 lines out of the views against
~280 in the component, so the net saving is modest. The point is that Rules 116,
122 and 136 stop being conventions checked in review. A `Cell func(T) string`
gives styled text nowhere to go; a single solver makes the width invariant
testable; `SetItems` is the only place a cursor can be left dangling.

What stays in the views: column definitions and their extractors, domain actions
(`ctrl+d`, `ctrl+s`, `enter`), tabs, forms, and the explorer's drill-down —
sorting and filtering already apply to the current level only.

#### Three that will not fit the config cleanly

- **`status`** — two tables sharing one viewport with alternating focus
  (`DefaultTableStyles` / `BlurredTableStyles` per tab, `update.go:364-371`).
  Two `datatable.Model` plus a focus helper, not a multi-table abstraction.
- **`security/findings`** — filters by tab *and* severity before the text query,
  and resets the cursor to the top on tab change (`findings.go:53`), which is the
  opposite of what `SetItems` should do by default. Needs an explicit reset call.
- **`netdiag` ports** — the lazy rebuild (`tableReady` / `lastTableWidth`,
  `ports_model.go:346-378`) exists to keep scroll position across a 2 s tick.
  That is exactly what `SetItems` must guarantee, so the code goes away — but it
  is the migration step that has to prove it.

#### Suggested order

One view per PR, risk ascending:

1. `datatable` plus tests (width invariant, clamp, sort, filter) — no view migrated
2. `oci_resources` networks + volumes — simplest, no sort
3. `netdiag` ports — proves scroll preservation on live data
4. `containers`, then `oci_resources` images — prove sort, arrows, `RowState`
5. `workspaces`, `explorer` — prove clamp and drill-down
6. `security`, `status` — the two special cases

Step 1 is worth landing on its own: the width solver and its test pin the
invariant before any view depends on it, which is the ordering the phase-3
coverage work already showed pays off (surface tests, then move, then complete).

Not started. Nothing here is settled; the API sketch is a proposal, and the open
question is whether `RowState` is enough to cover `TableStylesForSeverity` in
`security` without the component learning about severity.

Ajouté : `docs/backlog.md:906`, section **2. Technical debt**, entre « Files over the 800-line ceiling » et « Race detector cannot run locally » — c'est de la dette structurelle, pas une feature, donc §2 plutôt que §3.

L'entrée (146 lignes) contient :

- **L'inventaire** — 15 tables / 8 packages, et ce qui est déjà partagé (styles, `FilterBar`, `TimeAgo`) versus ce qui ne l'est pas.
- **Le tableau des duplications** — 6 axes avec le nombre de copies et les `fichier:ligne` exacts des 12 sites de calcul de largeur, des 3 comparateurs de tri, des 3 blocs de flèches, des 5 boucles de filtre, des 9 `getSelectedX()`.
- **La classe de défaut chiffrée** — les clamps `max(…, floor)` appliqués *après* le calcul du reliquat cassent l'invariant Rule 116. Chiffré sur `workspaces` : sous 154 colonnes la somme vaut 130 contre un `available` de 96 à width=120, soit 34 de débordement. Même classe à `security/findings.go:143`, `registry_browser.go:240` (dernière colonne potentiellement négative), `oci_resources/layout.go` ×4, `ports_model.go:325`.
- **Le couplage curseur/pipeline** — pourquoi les `getSelectedX()` sont la duplication à supprimer pour des raisons de correction, pas de volume.
- **L'API proposée** — `internal/ui/datatable`, avec la justification des génériques (`bubbles/table` prend des `[]string`, donc une config déclarative seule ne peut pas remonter au type métier).
- **Les 3 cas qui ne rentrent pas** — `status` (deux tables, focus alterné), `security` (reset curseur au changement d'onglet, opposé du comportement par défaut), `netdiag` ports (rebuild paresseux à prouver).
- **L'ordre de migration** en 6 étapes, avec le rappel que l'étape 1 se pose seule — même logique « surface tests, then split, then complete » que la phase 3 de couverture.

J'ai marqué explicitement `Not started. Nothing here is settled` avec la question ouverte (est-ce que `RowState` suffit pour `TableStylesForSeverity` sans que le composant apprenne ce qu'est une sévérité), pour rester cohérent avec la façon dont §3.8 sépare le réglé de l'ouvert.

Deux choses que je n'ai **pas** faites, à valider : le `Last Updated` en tête de fichier est déjà au 2026-08-04, donc inchangé ; et je n'ai pas ajouté de plan dans `.claude/plans/` — l'entrée backlog contient le design, mais si tu veux le plan d'implémentation détaillé de l'étape 1, c'est un document séparé.
